defects: The film is one 30 s locked-off shot. The camera never moves, reframes or changes scale, so 22 of 29 seconds read almost the same as the second before.

The year-by-year scrub (about 5.5–16.5 s) is the same move repeated about 38 times: the year number swaps, the ice outline shrinks slightly and the chart line extends one step. There's no change in rhythm, no acceleration into the 2012 record low and no hold where it matters.
The ice shape changes like a jittery mask. The year pair shows it shrinking evenly from frame to frame with no easing, no weight, and no sense of melt or material change.
The year numbers swap as hard cuts. Nothing rolls, eases or moves the type; only the digits change.
The final 3 seconds are almost completely static (measured change is 0.0). It's an end card with no settle motion and no last beat.
The end card is a text slide over a dimmed map. It doesn't work as a poster image, and the source block in small monospace looks like a document page rather than a designed frame.
The Greenland overlay and the hatched loss ring both arrive in one transition, so two reveals land on the same beat and compete.
Small labels on the map and chart (1979, 2012, 8M/6M/4M, the source line) are around 9–10 px and low-contrast, which will turn to mush once the film is compressed for web delivery.
Sound: the tick sound repeats identically every year, with no variation in pitch or level as the ice declines, over a static pad that has a few steady harmonics and no development.
gaps: Choreography: the data needs to be staged as camera and editorial beats. The scrub could accelerate through the stable years, slam into 2012, hold, then release. Push the camera in on the ice edge, cut between the map, the chart and the number, and give the ice a melt or erosion behaviour with weight instead of a shrinking mask.

Sound design: the ticks should change with the data, for example getting lower or thinner as the ice falls. The pad needs to build in arrangement towards the -36% reveal, and the record low and the end card each need their own designed hit. Right now there is one swell over sustained tones, with a long tail and an end card that does nothing.

Finish and ending: the end needs a designed final frame. The ghosted ice could resolve into the 1979 ring, rhyming with the opening and leaving an image people remember. The micro-labels also need hierarchy and contrast so they survive the delivery codec.
